paper_metadata.title: High temperature mechanical behavior of Nb-Mo-ZrC alloys

evidence.quote: The microstructure and mechanical behavior of several Nb-Mo-ZrC alloys were investigated from room to elevated temperatures.
All alloys, each about 25 g, were prepared by arc-melting under argon.
The ingots were homogenized at 2073 K for 24 h in an argon atmosphere, followed by furnace cooling.
the microstructure of these alloys consisted of a solid solution (Nb, Mo)ss phase with A2 structure
the microstructure is composed of primarily-solidified ZrC and eutectic of Mo and ZrC
the microstructure is composed of primarily-solidified ZrC and eutectic of Mo and ZrC
Both alloys exhibit a hyper-eutectic structure.

the improvement of strength in the Nb-Mo-ZrC alloy is mainly attributed to solid solution strengthening of the matrix. It is obvious the Mo exhibits a strong solid solution strengthening effect on the strength of (Nb, Mo)ss.
